questions.question: In Kabaddi, a super tackle is when a raider is caught/self out/declared out with or less than how many defenders defending?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A super tackle in Kabaddi is when a raider is caught/self out/declared out with three or fewer defenders defending.
 
• This rule adds an extra point to the defending team’s score for successfully tackling the raider under these conditions.
 
• It is a strategic advantage for the defending team as it not only prevents the raider from scoring but also boosts their own score.
 
• Super tackles are crucial in turning the tide of the match, especially when the defending team is outnumbered.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India and is popular in many South Asian countries.
 
• The game is played with two teams of seven players each, and the objective is for a single raider to tag members of the opposing team and return to their own half without being tackled.
 
• A match consists of two halves, typically 20 minutes each, with a 5-minute break in between.
 
• The sport requires a combination of strength, strategy, and agility, making it both exciting and challenging.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the Badminton game and match length?

options.text: A match consists of the best of four games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of two games of 21 points.
A match consists of the best of five games of 21 points.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A match in badminton consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
 
• The first player or pair to reach 21 points wins the game, provided there is a minimum lead of 2 points.
 
• If the score reaches 20-20, the game continues until one player or pair gains a 2-point lead (e.g., 22-20, 23-21).
 
• If the score reaches 29-29, the first player or pair to reach 30 points wins the game.
 
• The winner of a match is the first to win two games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).
 
• The sport can be played in singles (one player per side) or doubles (two players per side).
 
• Badminton became an Olympic sport in 1992 at the Barcelona Games.
 
• The court dimensions for singles and doubles are different, with the doubles court being wider.
 
• Players must serve diagonally across the court to their opponent.
 
• The serve must be underhand and the shuttlecock must be hit below the server's waist.

questions.question: In kabaddi, when a raider touches any body part of any defender or any part of their clothing, it is called :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tag**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In kabaddi, when a raider touches any body part of any defender or any part of their clothing, it is called a **tag**.
 
• The raider's objective is to tag as many defenders as possible in a single raid and return to their half of the court without being caught.
 
• If the raider successfully tags a defender and returns to their half, the tagged defender is out.
 
• The game requires a combination of strength, strategy, and agility to tag defenders and evade being caught.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India.
 
• The game is played between two teams of seven players each, with the objective of scoring points by raiding into the opponent's court and tagging out as many defenders as possible.
 
• The sport has gained international popularity and is played in various countries across the world.
 
• Kabaddi is included in major international sporting events like the Asian Games.
 
• The game is known for its fast pace and requires a high level of physical fitness and strategic thinking.

questions.question: Fighting in the upright position in judo is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tachi-waza**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tachi-waza** refers to fighting in the upright position in judo.
 
• In judo, techniques are classified into different categories based on the position and method of execution.
 
• **Ashi-waza** involves foot techniques, **ne-waza** involves groundwork techniques, and **koshi-waza** involves hip techniques.
 
• **Tachi-waza** techniques are crucial as they form the basis for throwing an opponent while standing.
 
• Practitioners train extensively in tachi-waza to improve their balance, timing, and the ability to execute throws effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Judo was developed in Japan in 1882 by Jigoro Kano, emphasizing the principles of maximum efficiency and mutual welfare and benefit.
 
• The sport is governed by the International Judo Federation (IJF), which organizes competitions and sets the rules for international judo.
 
• Judo has been an Olympic sport since 1964, showcasing a variety of throwing and grappling techniques.
 
• Training in judo not only improves physical fitness but also promotes discipline, respect, and mental fortitude.
 
• Judo practitioners, known as judokas, wear a uniform called a judogi and train on a mat called a tatami.

questions.question: As per Olympic rules, in the third game, badminton players change ends when a side scores _____ points.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11 points**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per **Olympic rules**, badminton players change ends in the third game when a side scores **11 points**.
 
• This rule is in place to ensure fairness by mitigating the effects of any environmental factors such as wind or lighting that could favor one side of the court.
 
• The rule applies to both singles and doubles matches in badminton.
 
• Players also change ends at the end of the first game and at the end of the second game if a third game is to be played.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Badminton World Federation (BWF)** is the international governing body for the sport of badminton.
 
• According to the **BWF regulations**, the change of ends helps to maintain the balance and fairness of the game.
 
• The current scoring system in badminton is the 21-point rally scoring system, where players score a point on every serve, regardless of which side is serving.
 
• The BWF regularly updates the rules and regulations to enhance the sport and ensure fair play.

questions.question: The term 'header' is associated to which of the following sports?

__

• This can be **done by standing, jumping, or diving position.**
 
• The header is a **common technique **and is used by players in almost every match.
 
• A** forward uses a header to score a goal.**
 
• A **defender uses a header to prevent the scoring of a goa**l by the opponent. 
 
• A header is the only option when the ball is in the air, because of the rule that a player can’t make contact with the ball using their hands.
 
• Most header goals are scored as a result of a cross or a corner. 
 
• **Tim Cahill, Marco van Basten, and Cristiano Ronaldo **are some players who are notable for their quality headers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• After the first 45 minutes, players will take a **15-minute rest period called half time.**

• The team that has scored more goals at the end of the game is the winner.
 
• If both teams have scored an equal number of goals then the game is a draw.

questions.question: The term ‘banana kick’ is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Football**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'banana kick'** is associated with the sport of **Football**.
 
• A banana kick is a type of kick that curves or bends in the air, typically used in free kicks and corner kicks.
 
• This technique is often used to navigate around defensive walls or to place the ball into the goal from a challenging angle.
 
• Famous footballers known for their banana kicks include legends like **David Beckham** and **Roberto Carlos**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The physics behind a banana kick involves imparting spin to the ball, resulting in a curved trajectory due to the **Magnus effect**.
 
• Mastering the banana kick requires significant skill, practice, and an understanding of ball dynamics.
 
• This technique adds a strategic element to the game, allowing players to create scoring opportunities from set pieces.

questions.question:

I. Batting - Cricket

II. Goal - Netball
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II.**__

• **Terms related to cricket.**

 
 

 Term
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Batting
 The act of hitting the ball with the bat in an attempt to score runs.
 
 

 Bowling
 The action of the player throwing the ball towards the wicket defended by the batsman.
 
 

 Run
 The basic unit of scoring in cricket, achieved by batsmen running between the wickets.
 
 

 Wicket
 The set of stumps and bails; also refers to the dismissal of a batsman.
 
 

 Over
 A set of six deliveries bowled by the same bowler from the same end of the pitch.
 
 

 Innings
 The period in which a team or a batsman is at bat.
 
 

 Duck
 A score of zero by a batsman.
 
 

 Century
 A score of 100 runs by a batsman in a single innings.
 
 

 Maiden Over
 An over in which no runs are scored off the bowler's deliveries.
 
 

 Out
 The condition when a batsman is dismissed from play.
 
 

 
• **Terms related to Netball.**

 
 

 Term
 Definition
 
 
 
 

 Goal
 A successful shot in the opponent's net, worth one point.
 
 

 Centre Pass
 The method of starting and restarting play at the beginning of each quarter and after a goal is scored.
 
 

 Wing Attack
 The position that links the attack and centre court, feeding the ball to the shooters.
 
 

 Goal Circle
 The semi-circular area in front of each goal from within which goals may be scored.
 
 

 Footwork
 The rule that states a player may land and then pivot on one foot while in possession of the ball.
 
 

 Free Pass
 A pass awarded after an infringement by the opposing team.
 
 

 Offside
 An infringement that occurs when a player moves out of their designated area.
 
 

 Penalty Pass
 A free pass awarded where the infringement occurred.
 
 

 Pivot
 A player using one foot as a swivel while moving the other foot in any direction.
 
 

 Throw in
 A method of restarting play when the ball has gone out of court.

questions.question: The term 'dribble' is used in which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basketball.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The term** 'dribble'** is used in **Basketball.**
 
• In basketball, dribbling is bouncing the ball on the floor continuously with one hand at a time.
 
• It is the only legal way that a player may maintain possession of the ball while walking or running.
 
• The dribble allows for much faster advancement and thus more opportunities for scoring.
 
• It also provides an opportunity for a crafty player on the opposing team to "steal" the ball in mid-bounce.
 
• Dribbling **should be done with finger pads** and the fingers should be relaxed and spread.
 
• The wrist should be pushing the basketball, and the forearm should be moving up and down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Basketball is a team sport in which there are two teams of five players each.
 
• Players advance the ball by bouncing it while walking or running (dribbling) or by passing it to a teammate.
 
• On offense, players may use a variety of shots – **the layup, the jump shot, or a dunk; on defense.**
 
• They may steal the ball from a dribbler,** intercept passes, or block shots; either offense or defense **may collect a rebound.
 
• It is a violation to lift or drag one's pivot foot without dribbling the ball, to carry it, or to hold the ball with both hands and then resume dribbling.

questions.question: In Equestrian sports, ______ occurs when a horse or rider lowers an element of a jump that establishes the height of an obstacle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**knockdown**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Knockdown** occurs when a horse or rider lowers an element of a jump that establishes the height of an obstacle in equestrian sports.
 
• This typically results in penalties for the rider, affecting their overall score in the competition.
 
• A knockdown is often caused by the horse's legs hitting the jump or the rider's mistakes in guiding the horse over the obstacle.
 
• It is a common term used in show jumping and other equestrian events involving jumps.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equestrian sports** include a variety of disciplines such as show jumping, dressage, eventing, and more.
 
• In **show jumping**, riders and their horses are required to jump a series of obstacles within a set time.
 
• Penalties are given for faults such as knockdowns, refusals, and exceeding the time limit.
 
• The goal is to complete the course with the fewest penalties and the fastest time.
 
• Proper training and understanding between the rider and horse are crucial for success in these events.
